goal: Acquire one radial-field (Br) SHARP CEA map per development HARP-day so that a later, separately frozen protocol can test whether image information raises window precision at the project operating point (config/operating-point-v2.json). This file covers acquisition only; it defines no model, no candidate and no acceptance rule.

scope.cadence: one record per HARP per day at T_REC 00:00:00 TAI
scope.selection: HARP-days that contain at least one development forecast window in the frozen shards
scope.reserved_period: No record with T_REC on or after 2024-01-01 is indexed or requested. The reserved 2024-2025 test stays closed.

measured_before_download.calibration: 40 HEAD requests, pooled 1.653 compressed bytes per pixel, range 1.139-2.907

processing.resize: area mean over valid pixels (adaptive average of values divided by adaptive average of the validity mask); cells with no valid pixel are stored as 0
processing.dtype: float16, gauss, no clipping or normalisation
processing.kept_per_map: raw sha256, raw bytes, original width and height, NaN fraction, T_REC
processing.raw_files: deleted after hashing and resizing because free disk space is about 12 GB

availability_rule_for_later_use: A map with record time T_REC may be used only by forecast windows at least 24 hours after T_REC unless a later protocol documents a shorter measured publication latency. The acquisition does not attach maps to windows.
limits: One map per day means a window can see a map that is up to about two days old under the 24-hour rule.
Resizing to a fixed shape changes the pixel scale differently for each HARP; original dimensions are kept so a later protocol can account for it.
JSOC storage paths can go offline; unavailable records are listed in the manifest and never imputed.
